author: Nana Kwame Adjei-Brenyah
comments: I did not think I would like a science fiction book about killing this much. It was essentially perfect. The characters were so well developed, it was compellingly written and readable. Somehow unlike what I normally read, but at the very base, exactly like what I normally read.

author: Miranda July
comments: I re-read this after about a decade and I still loved it. It's weird but insightful, and the uncomfortable parts make some sort of sense.

author: Katherena Vermette
comments: This was sort of continuation and an expansion of her other two books. It felt a little forced, a little unrealistic and a bit of a, I need to progress the story type book. I still liked it, but no where near as much ad the others. Also, if you hadn't read the others this would be very hard to follow.

author: Gordon Neufeld
comments: It's about how important the parent kid relationship is, and how we shouldn't push peers. I learned a lot but also felt preached to. It was a big heavy handed.

author: Coco Mellors
comments: I really liked it, it's about 4 sisters but one died. Written from the 3 others perspectives. They made the dead one into a bit of a Saint, but I guess that's accurate. Well developed characters, even if their trauma wasn't well fleshed out.

author: Rachel Khong
comments: I liked the premise, and most of the story but the science part felt too far fetched and made the rest seem a little silly. I also hate this kind of ending that sort of resolves things but not really.

author: Claire Lombardo
comments: Really readable, and good at jumping around in time. It was about motherhood, being in a long term relationship and how you evolve. I really felt seen for some parts, and overall I really liked it.

author: Amy Griffin
comments: I wanted to like this so much more than I did. It was good but the writing just didn't capture me even though the subject matter should have. The reveal

author: Charlotte Wood
comments: It's about an atheist who joins an abbey. I liked it but it petered out towards the end. I'd like to know why she joined and it didn't really tell you that.

author: Catherine Hernandez
comments: I really liked the main story, but the vehicle she used to tell it felt like a bit of a sloppy stretch. I think she could have done it without the serial killer, or the victim the main character knew tangentially.

bookTitle: What your are looking for is in the library
author: Michiko Aoyama
comments: These were short interconnected stories about different Japanese people who were feeling lost in some way. I liked some more than others, but it was charming and quick.

author: Allen Eskens
comments: It started so strong and ended so bad. In that way it reminded me of an Australian one I read. It devolved into over the top murder shit. It started really well written, and this college kid who was writing about a convicted murderer. But it was too much, and honestly got a bit silly. I skimmed the last 1/3.

bookTitle: 10 minutes 38 seconds in this strange world
author: Elif Shafak
comments: I really liked the first half, the second half felt rushed and flat. The main character was really well developed until she just wasn't, and the friend relationships weren't very well fleshed out, and after Leila died, it focused too much on them.

author: Clare Leslie Hall
comments: It was suspenseful as long as you didn't linger and think about it for too long. The writing was propelling and you were invested in the characters. I sort of knew a bunch of it because it was was a little obvious, but it didn't really matter.

author: Billy-Ray Belcourt
comments: I'm not 100% sure this book is as good as my rating, it might have just landed for me at the perfect time. I loved the stories, each about a different indigenous person and experience. The writing felt gentle and thoughtful to me, and really though provoking.

bookTitle: I hope this finds you well
author: Natalie Sue
comments: I went to high school with the author, which is why I read it. It's was funny, very readable - but the HR trope was a bit much, and a bit silly. The traumatic incident also just didn't land completely for me.

author: Elizabeth Renzetti
comments: This is a feminist examination of some of the issues on the world today. It was well written and readable, I loved it to much. From care giving to Taylor swift to domestic violence. I devoured it.

author: Daniel Mason
comments: It's a story about a house spanning hundreds of years and the people who live in it. I loved the first 2/3, but the last part fell off for me. I liked the idea of the ending, but didn't care enough about the person it happened to.

author: Oliver Burkeman
comments: I really liked this, although it was a tiny bit repetitive. The average person has 4000 weeks to live, and this book talks about how to really feel like you're living them. The crux of it is how to realize you'll never get everything done, and that once you figure that out you will stop feeling like you need to cram everything 8n to get to the ideal state. The ideal state is now bc that's where you are.

author: Carlos Ruiz Zafon
comments: I really liked this book to start, but the last 1/3 was a bit too up it's own butt. The writing was pretenscious, and felt sort of formulaic? I did love one of the characters a lot though.

author: John Green
comments: It was actually about what it sounds like it's about - how TB shaped our world, and continues to do so. It's about health inequities, how it shaped beauty standards that still exist today. Informative and very readable.

author: Charlotte McConaghy
comments: Some of the plot was a little far fetched, but it draws you in so much it doesn't matter. The characters and environment are really fleshed out, and you're rooting for all of them, including the island. It was the fastest I've read a book in a long time.

bookTitle: The Life Cycle of the Common Octopus
author: Emma Knight
comments: It was fine, first half better than the second. I called the "mystery" which is annoying. There was a bit too much going on, too many characters you were supposed to care about.

author: Richard Powers
comments: I am so torn on what to rate this book. The description of the ocean makes me almost desperate to go diving again. It was really beautifully written, and I loved the woman diver character. However the weird twist, almost haha it was all a dream thing at the end wasn't well executed, and left me confused. I think one portion was a main character narrarating, and the other was AI telling him his own story with gaps filled in back to him, but I'm not sure. There were also some weird points with cultural appropriation.

author: Evan Osnos
comments: I loved this book so much. It was well written and accessible, and super interesting on the true affluent in the world. It's maddening to have this kind of wealth disparity, especially when governments have the ability to fix it.

author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
comments: This is a novel from different perspectives of 4 women with interwoven lives during covid. The main woman's story was the start and I really liked her, and the next, but it got worse from there, and by the end I was skimming.

bookTitle: The Three Stigmata of Palmer Eldritch
author: Philip K Dick
comments: I wanted to like it more than I did. I liked the fact it's a relatively old book that seems almost prescient on climate change, but I also rarely like old books in general. The characters weren't developed, decisions seemed to come out of left field, and the female characters were just written to serve a purpose. It was supposed to be mind bending, and maybe it was a little, but I just didn't care.

author: William Stixrud and Ned Johnson
comments: About how to cede control and let your kid take charge of their own life. Sometimes the advice felt a little idealistic, but overall it landed for me that were consultants, not bosses. They want to have a good life, and it's our job to help them figure out fof themselves the best path to do that.

author: Souvankham Thammavongsa
comments: I was disappointed, it just didn't catch me. I loved her short stories, and I liked the idea of following a character for one day, but it didn't make me feel much at all.

author: Dennis Lehane
comments: This book was compulsively readable but definitely not my normal genre. It was violent, and although the main character got some redemption, it wasn't as much as you want her to get., white author writing about racial issues, is different from what I have been reading lately. I'm not sure I think the use of the n word is appropriate. It would have been starred out.

author: Liza Ridzen
comments: It's a quiet, slow moving book where not much happens, about aging, family and death. A son wants to take his dads dog away as he gets older. It's easy to read and I read it really quickly.

author: Curtis Sittenfeld
comments: I actually don't know why I loved this so much, maybe because it externalized feelings that are usually internal? Said the quiet part out loud?

author: Chelsea Bieker
comments: I loved this book until she met "Jane". It just took too unbelievable of a turn for me then, in a few different ways.

author: Joshua Whitehead
comments: I liked some of the stories, they were all future focused through an indigenous perspective after some sort of apocalypse. They felt repetitive though.

author: Brian Thomas Isaac
comments: This book took a while to draw me in, and the writing style was really different. They didn't really expand on how any characters felt, I was left to interpret it sort of. I thought I didn't like it but I think I did. I found the ending very powerful.

author: Ocean Vuong
comments: I wanted to like it more than I did. It had all the right ingredients for me; queer main character, family issues, addiction stuff... Intergenerational friendship, but it fell flat and I skimmed.

author: Anne Tyler
comments: This was a light, easy enjoyable read. I think I needed something like this and might have dared on the higher end because of that! It's set over 3 days from the moms perspective, when her daughter is getting married.

author: Christina Wong and Daniel Innes
comments: I think if I was more familiar with Toronto I would have enjoyed this more. It's about an tenderly Chinese woman whose husband dies. The book covers her life after and her memories. It's got really great descriptions of place, but I normally enjoy those more when they're familiar.

author: Emily Austin
comments: I liked the idea of it more than I liked the execution. It's about 2 sisters, who don't like of understand each other, but they had a rough upbringing that bonds them. One tries to die by suicide, the is left with it all to deal with. The end is well done.

author: Eddy Boudel Tan
comments: It was a propulsive read and I really liked the setting (north of Powell river). I didn't see the reveal coming, which is nice for once! The after math of it seemed odd to me though, a little too happy, maybe?

author: Virginia Evans
comments: The book is a series of letters that tells the story of the latter part of a woman's life. It made me cry, and also made me wish I wrote letters.

bookTitle: The Sirens' Call: How Attention Became the World's Most Endangered Resource
author: Chris Hayes
comments: It's about the history on attention, and how attention works and how it's shifted over the years. Its fascinating an depressing, I felt like the solutions were lacking a little bit maybe the author doesn't know any.

author: Catherine Chidgey
comments: It's a book from the perspective of a magpie who gets saved after falling out of its nest as a baby. A woman adopts him, her husband is abusive and her family isn't really that supportive even though they're close. It's sad, weird, and I really liked it. I didn't like the kidnapping part but it wasn't too long.

author: Caro Claire Burke
comments: It's about a religious woman who becomes an influencer. It's propulsive, readable and interesting! Very

author: Sophie Gilbert
comments: It looks at how awful the 2000/2010s were for women. It goes over how the 90s started something, then the 2000s wiped it out. It was insightful and interesting, especially given how I could put it in thrconte t of my own life, but it went on a bit.

author: Annie Hartnett
comments: Sweet but a big formulaic and predictable. It treats tragedy and death a little lightly, but I think it mostly worked.

author: Sarah Damoff
comments: It's about a couple, then a family. Alcoholism is a big theme too. There were a few parts that felt pivotal that I felt were underexplained (starting to drink and a death) , but overall I really liked it.

bookTitle: One Day, Everyone Will Have Always Been Against This
author: Omar El Akkad
comments: I loved this so much. It's about the authors life, and about the Israel Palestine conflict and how the world so easily turns away. And that we will only return to looking at it once we have a safe distance from it and can tutt tutt like we acted outraged all along.

author: David Szalay
comments: I'm surprised I enjoyed this as much as I did. I found it insightful in a way I didn't think I would because it seemed very male. It's about a kid who struggles, a young adult who succeeds then falls back into struggle. It's melancholy and makes you consider life and how things happen.

author: Megha Majumdar
comments: I wanted this to be better than it was. I liked it but I wanted it to be over, sort of. The climates stuff was interesting, but the thief part felt a little forced.

author: Becky Chambers
comments: I liked it, didn't love it. It's about a gender neutral human and a robot bonding, and learning snout each other, and the human learning about nature - driven by a quest to hear crickets. They hear them at the end and I think it's supposed to be like a thrilling conclusion, but I thought it was annoying and a clear lead in for a sequel. Maybe I don't like world building when it's clearly in service of a follow up, I'm not sure.

bookTitle: The house of Sand and Fog
author: Andre Dubus III
BB Easton
comments: This was way too trashy for me. And about high school sex, it was just too ridiculous. Badly written. I only finished it bc I didn't have another one ready to go yet.

bookTitle: We so seldom look on love
author: Barbara Gowdy

bookTitle: the Beautiful things that heaven bears
author: Dinaw Mengestu

bookTitle: The art of racing in the rain
author: Garth Stein

bookTitle: a Sunday at the pool in Kigali
author: Gil Courtemarche

bookTitle: Colorless life of Tsukuru Tazaki and his years of pilgrimage
author: Haruki Murakami
Haruki Murakami
comments: no magical element

bookTitle: The final testament of the holy bible
author: James Frey

bookTitle: 100 year old man who climbed out the window
author: Jonas Jonasson

bookTitle: The Tale of the Unknown Island
author: Jose Saramago

bookTitle: The brief Wondrous life of oscar wao
author: Junot Diaz
Emily Henry
comments: Very fitting name, and it was just too much for me. Too trashy, too silly, too predictable. I skimmed a lot.

bookTitle: We need to talk about Kevin
author: Lionel Shriver

bookTitle: Senor Vivo and the coca lord
author: Louis de Bernieres

bookTitle: The curious incident of the dog in the night-time
author: Mark Hadden

bookTitle: no one belongs here more than you
author: Miranda July
Emma Cline
comments: It was fine, boring, I only finished these short stories bc nothing else was available.

bookTitle: The phone booth at the edge of the world
author: Laura Imai Messina
comments: i wanted this to be so much better than it was. the writing was blah, the story was blah. not worth reading.

author: TJ Klune
comments: this whole book was just too on the nose. the allegory between magical beings and poc and lgbtq, the language. i liked that the love story was just normal, but with 2 men, but it just tried too hard.

author: Ali Hazelwood
comments: I barely wanted to finish this, it was so formulaic, very traditional in terms of sexes. I skimmed a lot.

author: Celeste Ng
comments: It was fine. An ok look at feeling different and parental pressure, but it got boring and I skimmed. The death part felt unrealistic.

author: Emma Straub
comments: It was fine, very predictable and an easy read. The characters were under developed and that made it a little boring.

author: Amanda  Eyre ward
comments: I liked the premise for a beach read but it fell flat. Most of the family finding out way after the fact that the alcoholic dad commiting suicide was a weird footnote. It felt like it should have been more central. Not well written.

author: Stephen King
comments: The first half was really good, I liked the main character I liked the premise, but there is a twist in the middle and it just went shit from there. He writes women terribly and it's beyond frustrating. The characters around the woman are frustrating because of it.

author: Eric Walters
comments: this book was fine. It was not that well written, I just don't feel like he was writing from a teenager perspective, despite trying really hard. Sometimes the internal dialogue was painful.

author: Douglas Stewart
comments: About a family centered around an alcoholic mother in Ireland. It felt like tragedy porn instead of a sad story about people who are written to make you care about them. Character development was non-existent.

author: Billy-Ray Belcourt
comments: I like the idea of the poems, but it was a little too esoteric for me.

author: Catherine Gildner
comments: This book was fine, it was written by a therapist about what she thinks were her 5 most resilient clients. It felt like a weird sort of expose, tradedy porn sort of. I didn't like the writing style at all, and the stories were too much.

author: Angel Di Zhang
comments: This book was about a Chinese girl who moves to the US. I liked the idea, it centred around the mother daughter relationship. But the second half of the book tried too hard, felt put on and just fake poetic.

author: Mary Beth Keane
comments: Nowhere near as good as her first book. The subject matter wasn't as interesting, it was about a couple who hides financial trouble from each other, there is sort of an affair, someone helps someone disappear. Too much going on, bad character development. Readable but blah.

author: Lawrence Hill
comments: I really liked the idea of this book, but the fact that it wasn't using real country names, didn't work well for me. I also thought it got a little sensational, and the ending was all happy which doesn't seem realistic.

bookTitle: Things we lost in the fire
author: Mariana Enriquez
comments: really dark short stories, all with a horror/violent element. got repetitive.

author: Jasmine Guillroy
comments: spin off of the wedding date using different characters. not bad, but not really worth reading if you dont have a lot of time

author: Jasmine Guillroy
comments: spin off of the wedding date using different characters. not bad, but not really worth reading if you dont have a lot of time

author: Sally Rooney
comments: Interesting characters but the plot wasn't great

author: Jennifer Weiner
comments: Really liked the main character but the supporting characters were weird and sort of poorly written, and it turned into a murder mystery which I didn't expect or like

author: Peace Adzo Medie
comments: I kept waiting for it to get really good. It had potential but fell flat for me

author: Shani Mootoo
comments: Started really strong, really fell off. Switched points of view at one point (totally unnecessary) and the plot twists were obvious. There was too much going on, when it could have been a really neat story about feelings and how 2 different ppl view a situation.

author: Matt Haig
comments: A woman tries to mmcommit suicide then gets to try out all these different versions of her life. It was an interesting idea, but a little too rah rah appreciate the moment and all your opportunities for me. Heavy handed.

author: Elin Hildebrand
comments: very readable, addictive, but the maim premise has one of the main characters cheating on their spouse. i was supremely irritated they never left.

author: Mikki Kendall
comments: I liked it but it was a little repetitive. Really interesting, and great subject matter but maybe for my state of mind a little too academic.

author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
comments: I liked the characters and the writing was fine. It was about a family whose dad is very famous but mia and the mum dies young. It was good, easy to read, but I wasn't dying to know what happened next.

author: Sally Rooney
comments: i shouldn't read her stuff anymore. All too similar, this one was a miss for me. She doesn't write friendship as well as she writes relationships.

bookTitle: The stars and the blackness between them
author: Junauda Petrus
comments: This was fine, started well but I skipped a lot. Too much going on, and too young. I liked the black aspect but not enough.

author: Gideon Defoe
comments: The idea was so fun, and I learned a bit, but it was formulaic and repetitive.

author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
comments: This felt really dated. It was fine, and the African perspective was interesting, but it felt basic, probably only because of how much feminism has evolved since it was written.

bookTitle: The brilliant life of Eudora Honeysett
author: Annie Lyons
comments: This was about a crotchety old woman who has a vibrant 10 year old move in next to her. Very predictable, sweet moments. Boring.

author: Michelle Zauner
comments: a Korean American woman's mother dies. It's well written, but a bit self involved. And too much detail about food. The relationships are described really well.

author: Monica Ali
comments: This book was fine. It was a bit boring at times, and too long, and you sort of knew what would happen. I did like that the main character wasn't all that likeable. I did skim a lot.

author: Ashley Herring Blake
comments: This was chick lit, and came with the annoying type of writing that often does. It was enjoyable but predictable.

author: E. M. Tran
comments: I liked it to start, but less and less as ig moved away from the current day generation. The writing got worse and worse and I cared about the characters less and less. It was about vietnam, the war, and people having to leave. It was fine!

author: Samantha Irby
comments: She might be losing me a bit, I didn't find this anywhere near as funny as her last ones, and I skimmed a ton. Stuff funny parts, but overall missed the mark for me.

author: Shilpi Somaya Gowda
comments: It felt like it was supposed to be insightful, cutting commentary on privilege and racism but it felt a little formulaic, obvious and flat to me. I really liked her other books so I was disappointed.

author: Emma Staub
comments: This is about relationships, especially father daughter (single father essentially) and I liked it, but there was also a really dumb time travel element. At first I didn't mind it bc I could see what it was trying for but it was poorly done so it got old fast.

author: Haruki Murakami
comments: Started really strong but the ending was terrible. It's like the author had too many things on the go and just dropped too many balls for the story to feel cohesive at the end. It felt like the quality of the writing deteriorated as well. A good portion of this was a 10 for me, but the end was less than 5.

author: Helen Hoang
comments: Trashy but enjoyable

author: Colleen Hoover
comments: enjoyable easy read, very predictable.

author: Jasmine Guillroy
comments: Predictable easy summer read.

author: David Yoon
comments: YA, predictable, but still insightful and sweet

author: Sarah kay
comments: Easy to read book of poetry

author: Rupi Kaur
comments: insta poerty at its best, last third was the worst

author: Ocean Vuong
comments: Really beautifully written, but to the point where it got a little confusing and disjointed. Really lost focus 2/3 of the way through

author: Taffy Brodesser-Akner
comments: I struggle to rate this one. It's incredibly readable, super interesting topic, the writing was sometimes good, sometimes trying too hard. I liked the swith in point of views, but would have preferred it happen earlier. And the narration could be confusing at times.

author: Alka Joshi
comments: Pretty predictable, but still a good story. There were some unnecessary parts, and I feel like they tried to make the main character a tad unlikeable for being ambitious. Abortion was a central theme which I liked.

author: Yaa Gyasi
comments: It was about a girl whose brother dies of an overdose and her mom who is a single parent is depressed for the rest of her life, all which informs the girls life choices. It was good, but characters were barely introduced sometimes and left with no mention. Relationships weren't that well established.

author: Hazel Prior
comments: Lovely and a few really heartfelt surprisingly poignant parts, but maybe a little too predictable.

author: Ross Gay
comments: i loved the whole premise of this book, it was really addictive to read. I liked his voice in general but sometimes got a little lost in the sentences. A lot of them seemed like run ons. It made me smile a lot, and laugh a few times.

author: Roxanne Gay
comments: i really liked the writing and the topic, but there were a lot of references that were lost on me.

author: Omar El Akkad
comments: The ending was silly but I liked the rest. It's about refugees in Greece.

author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
comments: I liked it because I like her and I'm interested in grief. I can't stand when adults use the phrase daddy though.

author: Alan Weisman
comments: It looks back to predict what would happen to the world if humans were to disappear suddenly. It was really interesting, but a little repetitive. I learned quite a bit.

author: Cheluchi Onyemelukwe
comments: I would have liked this more without the kidnapping part. The stories of both women were interesting, and that prop to bring them together to learn about each other felt unnecessary. There had to be a better way.

author: Tea Mutonji
comments: Short stories but all about the same characters. Compelling but took me a long time to read for some reason.

bookTitle: We are never meeting in real life
author: Samantha Irby
comments: short essays about her life, very funny, but not as funny as the other one I read. She's very relatable and I like the way she writes.

author: Lisa Moore
comments: Good, but maybe would have been better if I'd had older kids? It's about love and different types of love, and I connected with some, but not all. And the main topic is a mom loving her 20 something year old.

author: Anosh Irani
comments: I wanted to like it more than I did. It's about eunuchs and sex trafficking. I didn't love the writing, and it felt a tiny bit disjointed but I did still enjoy it. It didn't end like I wanted it to/thought it would but it was close.

author: Shelby Van Pelt
comments: A tiny bit too predictable but still lovely. About an old lady whose son died, an octopus in an aquarium and a 30-ish year old guy. Very far fetched, but if you can let do of that it's much better.

author: George M Johnson
comments: The writing was a bit bad sometimes, but mostly fine. It was an in testing journey with a black queer kid through to university. I hated the part with the fraternity though. I'm sure it was very meaningful to the author but it just didn't connect for me, and since it was the end of the book, I was left feeling blah.

author: Kiley Reid
comments: This was good and very readable but some of the characters weren't very well developed so I had a hard time following why they made some decisions and did some things.

author: Tiffany D Jackson
comments: This was about black youth, female friendship and one of them disappears. The end was odd, the timelines were weird. I liked it, I didn't love it.

author: Dolki Min
comments: This is about an alien that gets stranded on earth and has sex with humans, then kills and eats them. It also touched on some queer themes but it got a bit repetitive.

author: Niigaan Sinclair
comments: This was non fiction about indigenous people and Winnipeg. It was good, but a bit repetitive. It could have been tightened up a little. I did learn quite a lot though!

author: Tove Jansson
comments: I spaced out a bit in certain parts of this. It's about a summer on an island for a grandmother and a granddaughter. It was sweet and funny, nice descriptions of place, but a bit underwhelming.

author: Amy Bloom
comments: Part of the novel was really interesting, navigating the right to die in the US and then having to go to Switzerland. The part I didn't like was the relationship between the author and her dying husband. She didn't flesh it out enough for me.

author: Holly Gramazio
comments: Fun concept, terrible last 1/4.

bookTitle: All the light we cannot see
author: Anthony Doerr
comments: Great 2 perspective story about WW II. Easy to read and captivating.

author: Tayari Jones
comments: loved the story and the style, not the end

author: Richard Van Camp
comments: quite a few were sort of short horror stories, but still enjoyable and really well written

author: Waubgeshig Rice
comments: well written, great story except for the ultimate climax; which was terrible.

author: Sigrid Nunez
comments: Really interesting perspective on losing someone and contemplating life and relationships

author: J Courtney Sullivan
comments: It was about 2 women at different stages of life, their relationship and their growth. I feel like the ending was realistic but I would have liked more resolution... Things coming to light or being solved or something. I also feel like some of the loose ends were just weird to leave hanging, but again, maybe that's realistic!

author: Thomas King
comments: a lovely story about an indigenous couple who go on vacations trying to find more information about one of their old family members. That part is really secondary though. It's mostly about their relationship, the man's inner problems. They name his demons and they are a little hard to keep track of to start. It's nicely written how it bounces between timelines but is never confusing.

bookTitle: 21 things you may not know about the indian act
author: Bob Joseph
comments: i learned a lot from this book. It was informative and readable if a little repetitive.

bookTitle: A history of my brief body
author: Billy-Ray Belcourt
comments: It's non fiction, about a indigenous person living/growing up in AB, mostly their perspectives on the world, Canada, being queer. It was very wordy sometimes, a bit much for my taste but I still really liked it.

author: Katherena Vermette
comments: I really liked it but found it a little heavy handed at the end. The family structure was a tiny bit confusing, and there were some loose ends that I didn't feel got tied up. The break was better. It was thought provoking and I think it will stay with me, the repercussions of seemingly small actions.

author: Jael Richardson
comments: It was a big allegory for residential schools/the treatment of indigenous folks. I thought it was fantastic, but a little heavy handed sometimes. Really well written and thought provoking though.

author: Yaa Gyasi
comments: i loved this book but found it a little hard to follow. Each chapter is the next generation down, and the links are hard to keep up with. Sometimes the characters felt a iny bit forced, but over all it was thought provoking, I learned quite a bit and I was emotionally attached to the through narrative of both sides of the family tree (even if I had trouble remembering which I was in).

author: Elaine Castillo
comments: I felt really deeply as I read this book, but there was one thing that bothered me, they left one important plot point with a main character dangling. It had to do with sexual abuse and I just don't understand why include if you aren't going to address it again really. It's about a large Filipino family and some of them coming over to the US. Characters are really well developed. I cried multiple times.

author: Tyler Feder
comments: graphic novel about someone's mom who dies. I cried a few times, sometimes it felt too specific for me to really connect with, but it was really well done.

author: Terese Marie Mailhot
comments: This was a memoir that talked about the indigenous experience, family, parents, sexual abuse, partners. It was really good but jumped around a little, and sometimes was a little too fancy literary style for me. It did really make you feel.

author: Gabrielle Zevin
comments: This was about video games, but not really. It was more about relationships (intimate and platonic), growing up... I really liked it but thought the character development of the main female could have been stronger.

author: David Benioff
comments: It was definitely YA, but I don't mind that. It's about a quest 2 boys go on in Russia when it's occupied by Germany in WW2. It was easy to read, comptempory even though it's not set in the present. It was sweet and drew you in.

author: William MacAskill
comments: It was about what we should be worried about now if we take a long term view for society, and what we can do about it. It was really good, a touch too optomistic for me maybe.

author: Ann Napolitano
comments: It  was about a complex family of 4 sisters, their parents, their kids, their love lives. Good, but not as good as her other one.

author: Michelle Good
comments: Non fiction about indigenous people in Canada. It was divided into different topics and was really interesting. Well written if a little repetitive.

author: Ashley Audrain
comments: Compulsively readable, about different experiences with motherhood. The ending was a little weird, and felt a bit reductive, but I still liked most of the book a lot.

author: Tommy Orange
comments: I loved it except the shooting at the ending. It was short stories kind of, but all tied together, and you have multiple stories following the same character. I thought the shooting must have been real but it wasn't... I guess it was an analogy for violence against indigenous people, even against themselves but it didn't quite land for me.

author: R F Kuang
comments: I really liked it until the end. It was just too much

author: Tanya Talaga
comments: This was about the problematic system of school indigenous youth outside of their home communities, specifically the ones who have to go go Thunder Bay. The only thing that I found hard about this book is there were a lot of characters and it didn't go as in depth into any of them as I would have liked.

author: David Graeber
comments: The reason I can't rate this higher is because it hit very close to home, and it got a little too long at the end. It deconstructed the types of jobs in the world, particularly useless ones. It talked about types of them, why they exist, how soul crushing they are. I loved it.

bookTitle: 13 ways of looking at a fat girl
author: Mona Awad
comments: Does an amazing job of speaking to body issues and female insecurity. I almost cried multiple times.

author: Katherena Vermette
comments: Great story, really well told except for the climax of the story. The end is also not the best, but I'm not sure what they should have done instead. Lots of multifaceted female characters. A litle hard to keep track of who is who, especially at the beginning.

author: Emma Straub
comments: very easy read, happy ending

author: Trent Dalton
comments: really beautifully written. the family/human story was phenomenal, the crime stuff started fine but got to be too much for me

author: Souvankham Thammavongsa
comments: Short stories about being the other, mostly based on Lao immigrant experience. Some really powerful stories about small moments.

author: Jacqueline Woodson
comments: I wish it was longer I think. But then maybe like in tv series it would have gotten worse? It was about a teen pregnancy from different perspectives... Sort of... Also about black identity... Sort of... The mother daughter relationship... Sort of. Hard to describe but really good.

author: Ann Napolitano
comments: I'm torn between 9 and 10 for this one. The sibling relationship was so well written and powerful, so was the death part at the end. The only part that I didn't love until the very end was the main friendship. I didn't dislike it, it just didn't seem that important somehow.

author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
comments: It was about a war in Nigeria when the country split in 2, Nigeria and Biafra, which I had never heard of! The only thing I might change is the timelines at the beginning are a tiny bit confusing. They also resolved everything except 1 main character and I really wish they'd just told us what happened to her.

author: Ashley Audrain
comments: This book was addictive. I had a very visceral reaction to it. I cried, I thought a lot about it. It would have been a 10 except I didn't like the last few paragraphs. I think it would have been better without them.

author: Samantha Irby
comments: Very funny, about normal life stuff, being around my age. It feels very honest and made me laugh out loud a lot. They are little essays, some of them felt a little less applicable, but they were still funny and I just skimmed a little more.

author: Francesca Ekwuyasi
comments: It's about Nigerian twins and their mother. One of them is raped at a young age and all of their lives form around that in different ways. There was a bit of sloppy writing and a few typos but otherwise I really liked how it was written.

author: Miranda Cowley Heller
comments: An addictive book about relationships. Complicated family stuff. The only thing that could have been better was a more decisive ending. I really liked the way it was written, the characters were well developed.

author: Kate Baer
comments: This was really simple, accessible, poetry; the only kind I like! She's a feminist but I did notice maybe her language could hand been more inclusive. Overall I still loved it and a lot of the poems resonated.

bookTitle: I hope this finds you well
author: Kate Baer
comments: Blackout poetry using feedback she received. It's really well done.

author: Elif Shafak
comments: A book about Cyprus through the lens of 2 young ppl in love, and a fig tree. It was beautiful, drew you in, taught you things about Cyrus and nature.

author: Ling Ma
comments: i started reading this and almost quit thinking it was written after the pandemic, and incredibly lazy. I checked before quitting and it was written in 2018! A virus from China has killed almost everyone and the time line goes between before and after. It eerily mirrored some things from the pandemic like n95s, traveler bans. I'm also watching the last of us, and the landscape there is like the landscape in the book except the zombies aren't harmful. It's a good commentary on capitalism. I loved it, not a 10 because there was an unnecessary pregnancy.

author: Thomas Curran
comments: This was commentary on perfectionism of all kinds, nicely supported by data. It looked at little issues and big issues, very plainly written.

author: Vincent Lam
comments: I read this more quickly than I've read anything in a long time. I loved it, I thought about it a lot. It's about the opiod crisis through a Dr and person who is addicted. It's hard to read as she goes through a bunch of stuff, the only thing is it felt like we missed learning something about her. Maybe that was the point?

author: Waubgeshig Rice
comments: This was a sequel to a book that I hated the ending of... So I was a bit worried. It was nothing like the other ending. It was about what happened to an indigenous community after a world ending catastrophe, and what they did. It was well written and descriptive without being too descriptive about the land. There were maybe too many characters, but I really liked it.

bookTitle: The memoirs of Miss chief eagle testickle: vol. 1
author: Kent Monkman, Gisele Gordon
comments: This was fun and informative to read. Colonialism from an indigenous perspective with truth and lots of humour mixed in. Lots of sexual content.

author: Catherine Hernandez
comments: A book about a Philipina worker who leaves her family to make money first in Hong Kong then canada. It's told from the perspective of her newborn baby, who has memories of being in the womb. It's about belonging, chosen family, transgender acceptance... I loved it and teared up a lot. I found the main character growth a tiny bit underdeveloped (like it just happened) but not a big deal.

author: Jonathan Haidt
comments: Nonfiction that talked about smart phones and Gen Z. It was super insightful in explaining why their childhood and early teen years were so different because of phones. It's depressing if nothing changes, but helped me think about how we raise our kids in terms of risk (of all types) and phones.

bookTitle: A Tale for the time being
author: Ruth Ozeki

bookTitle: I know this much is true
author: Wally Lamb
Catherine Hernandez
comments: Ensemble story of a neighbourhood in Toronto. It was so well written, made me cry multiple times. I loved it.

author: Mary beth Keane
comments: follows 2 families with intertwining lives, really well written and almost suspenseful? i loved it

bookTitle: The most fun we've ever had
author: Claire Lombardo
comments: slow moving family story with multiple characters and ages. they were well written and all likeable in some way. it was well written and the slow reveals were great.

bookTitle: Maybe you should talk to someone
author: Lori Gottlieb
comments: A book about therapy and ppl and how we live our lives and think about life and all the hard stuff. I found it especially poignant about death.

author: Brit Bennett
comments: Sort of a weird premise to start but so good. it's about different experiences being the other (mostly black) in the world. I almost don't want to give it 10 bc I loved it so much that I think the author could have done even better, but that's ridiculous.

author: Aimee Nezhukumatathil
comments: Short chapters about things in the natural world with the authors life woven in. A few times it got a little too sappy for my taste, but it was really really lovely overall. I didn't want to put it down, and I learned a few things. Really heartwarming.

author: Michelle Good
comments: It followed 5 children after they left residential schools. It was pretty heartbreaking even with the ones who ended up being being relatively ok. It was well written and readable.

author: Dayna Kukafka
comments: This is the most addicted to a book I have been in a long time. Really well written, thoughtful and almost suspenseful without being cheesy. All the characters were Multi dimensional. It was heartbreaking.

author: Tracey Lien
comments: I loved this so much. It was really well written, compulsively readable, and so compelling. It's sort of a mystery, and as it got revealed I thought I was going to be a bit disappointed. But you realize it doesn't even matter and that's not the point of the book.

author: Wolfgang Herrndorf
comments: YA at its best. Endearing, well written, sweet and funny.

bookTitle: The memoirs of Miss chief eagle testickle: vol. 2
author: Kent Monkman, Gisele Gordon
comments: This picks up where vol 1 left off, and I enjoyed it more because I knew more about what was going on. I cried multiple times, and it did such a beautiful job of walking through the history of North American colonialism. It loosely follows one family line, and the same main character who is the magical being. Lots of sexual content.

author: Naomi Klein
comments: Nonfiction about the state of the world (esp North America) post covid. It's framed around people confusing the author with Naomi Wolf, but it's so much more than that. It got a tiny bit dry with the historical stuff, but I learned a lot. It's insightful into why people think they way they think and how they believe what they believe.

author: Miranda July
comments: This book was SO weird. A novel about women and middle age, sexual crisis, I loved it. Captivatingly written, thought provoking. I can't really describe it. It spoke to me although I didn't fully connect with all of the sexual parts.

author: Janika Oza
comments: I cried at multiple points in this book, but there was also underlying joy. It was about an Indian family and how they got to Uganda, then how they had to leave. The relationships were well developed, realistic and carried throughout the book.
